copies.headline: Still First, Still Coasting Downhill
copies.body: Adam remains No. 1 because the math refuses to look anywhere else: 139.6 per game, first of twelve, and a 66-22 all-play that says 6-2 is if anything a discount. That said, two straight losses and a last-three stretch of 132.7, 103.0, 108.9 — 52% all-play, sixth of twelve — is the first time all year his floor has shown up uninvited. Luck is dead even, so nobody got robbed. The roster still projects 134 a week, best in the league, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Kenneth Walker III carrying. Mr. Consistent being inconsistent is new.

copies.headline: John's Rams Stack Is Doing Everything
copies.body: The 5-3 record undersells it: John's all-play is 61-27, 69%, 2nd of 12, and his 133.0 per game is also 2nd of 12. Luck sits at -0.5, meaning he's actually been scoring his way out of wins, not into them. The last three weeks — 100.1, 127.7, 165.1 — produced a 24-9 all-play. Puka Nacua projects 24 next week, Brock Bowers 18, Kyren Williams 17, and the whole thing hums at 125 a week, 3rd of 12. A draft-night grade of 80, T-9th, and he's here anyway. Big brother business as usual.

copies.headline: Christian Scores Like a Contender, Loses Like a Bystander
copies.body: Christian is 3-5 and it's close to fraudulent in the other direction. He's averaging 126.5 a game, 3rd of 12, with a 54-34 all-play — 61%, T-3rd — and he's sitting 1.9 wins below expectation, T-11th-luckiest of 12. The last three weeks are a metronome: 124.3, 122.3, 123.5, good for a 70% all-play. His draft board graded out at 89, T-2nd of 12, and the roster still projects 131 a week, 2nd of 12. CeeDee Lamb and George Kittle aren't the problem. The schedule is.

copies.headline: Logan Is 3-5 And Robbed Blind
copies.body: Logan is 3-5 and it's a crime scene. 979.1 points for, 122.4 a game, fourth in the league — and 1075.7 against, the most anyone has absorbed. All-play 54-34, luck minus 1.9. Over the last three weeks he's gone 152.5, 118.9, 146.4 and posted an 82% all-play, best in the league for that stretch. Burrow, Jefferson, McMillan: the scoring is real. The man who took two #1 seeds and won nothing now can't buy a win he's earned. Week 9 projects 118 against CJ.

copies.headline: Six-And-Two On Fumes And Favors
copies.body: Leif is 6-2 with a four-game win streak, which sounds like a contender until you notice the all-play is 43-45 and the luck is +2.1 wins, the luckiest mark of the twelve. Points against of 879.1, second-fewest, has done a lot of heavy lifting. The last three weeks are the problem: 112.3, 92.9, then 64.7, a season low, for a 10-23 all-play stretch that's 11th of 12. Christian McCaffrey and Mike Evans are both questionable. The roster projects 120 a week, sixth. Noah's up next, and Noah doesn't care about your record.

copies.headline: Grant Is Exactly 4-4, No Argument
copies.body: Grant sits at 4-4 with a 42-46 all-play, 114.8 a week, luck of plus-0.2 — which is to say the record isn't a trick, it's just who he is. The last three weeks have been genuinely good, 21-12 all-play, built on a 158.6 in Week 7 that looks like an outlier next to the 84.4 in Week 3. The concern is the roster index at 39 and a 113-a-week projection, 10th of 12. Amon-Ra St. Brown and Mahomes are carrying a lot. Week 9 is Adam. Good luck with that.

copies.headline: CJ Rises Two Spots Scoring Ninety
copies.body: CJ moved up two places by doing nothing in particular, which is the most Taylor Gang thing imaginable. Back-to-back duds of 90.9 and 95.1 have the last three weeks at 36% all-play, T-9th of 12, and the season average sits at 111.2, 8th in the league. The 4-4 record is honestly earned — luck is +0.4, basically neutral. Jonathan Taylor and Chuba Hubbard are a real backfield, but Mason Taylor at 8 projected points is a tight end in the loosest sense. Week 9 projects 115 against Logan.

copies.headline: 4-4 On Vibes And A Schedule
copies.body: Isaac is 4-4 and riding a two-game streak, which sounds fine until you see the all-play: 31-57, 35%, 11th of 12. That's the real number. The 104.8 per game is 11th too, and the only reason the record isn't ugly is 906.3 points against, 6th-fewest, plus +1.2 wins of luck. The roster says this shouldn't be happening — 123 a week projected, 5th of 12, with Ja'Marr Chase, Nabers and Saquon. Week 6's 79.0 is the honest version. Week 9 is Peter. Score something.

copies.headline: Best Draft On Paper, Worst Roster Going Forward
copies.body: Peter won draft night — 89 out of 100, first of twelve — and he's been coasting on it ever since. The 5-3 record is a costume: all-play is 40-48, luck is +1.4 wins, and points against are the 4th-fewest in the league. Over the last three weeks he's gone 12-21 all-play with a 69.8 somewhere in there, which is how a Week 4 163.0 team ends up here. The roster projects 101 a week, 12th of 12. Lamar Jackson is OUT. Enjoy 5-3 while it lasts.

copies.headline: Noah's Cinderella Window Is Closing Fast
copies.body: Noah's 143.1 in Week 8 was the first time all season this roster looked like it belonged, and it still only pushed him to 2-6. The context is uglier than the record: 107.5 a game, 9th of 12, an all-play mark of 33-55 that says the losses are earned, not stolen. Luck is -1.0, so there's a sliver of a case, but 38% is 38%. The postseason assassin reputation requires reaching the postseason. Drake Maye and James Cook III project 120 against Leif. Start there.

copies.headline: 5-3 Is A Magic Trick, Not A Team
copies.body: Kaleb is 5-3 with the fewest points against in the league and 103.4 a game, which is 12th of 12. That's not a résumé, that's a schedule. The all-play is 34-54, 39%, and luck sits at +1.9 wins — second-luckiest of 12 — so nearly two of those wins belong to the bracket, not the lineup. Week 8's 62.7 was the floor finding itself. The draft graded 86, T-4th of 12, and the roster index is 21, which is the whole story: Goff, London and Jeanty, then silence. 108 projected against Christian.

copies.headline: Nico Found, Everything Else Still Missing
copies.body: Mitchell's roster projects for 124 a week, fourth-best in the league, and he's averaging 106.9. That gap is the whole story. The 30-58 all-play is last of twelve, and the last three weeks — 85.5, 79.4, 108.5 — produced a 5-28 all-play, also last. This isn't bad luck; he's minus-1.7 wins, meaning he's underperforming his own bad scores. Gibbs projects 26, Golden 17, Kelce is still here. The 85 draft grade bought him a 1-7 record and a dress fitting. Week 9 is John.

intro: Adam stays at the top and it isn't close: 139.6 a game, a 75% all-play mark, and a 6-2 record built with exactly zero luck equity, which is the annoying part for everyone else. At the bottom sits Mitchell, 1-7 with a 15% form rating, though 106.9 a game and a -1.7 luck figure suggest he's been bad and unlucky rather than simply bad — his 127 projection is the highest in the bottom four. The week's loudest fall is Leif, down from third to fifth despite also being 6-2, because a 49% all-play, a 30% form number and +2.1 in luck is a 116.0-per-game team wearing Adam's record. Kaleb's slide from eighth to eleventh is the same story with worse ingredients: 103.4 a game, a 39% all-play, and +1.9 in luck holding up a 5-3 that nobody believes.
